assessments.reasoning: The exact dated W3C HTTPS location identifies the 26 November 2008 Fifth Edition Recommendation and matched the pinned SHA-256. The cited section anchors resolve in the freshly acquired bytes. Section 2.10 uses MUST for passing non-markup characters to the application and adds a reporting duty for validating processors. Section 4.4.2 defines included replacement text as processed at the location of the reference, with character data and markup treated by their ordinary rules. Section 4.4.3 conditions external parsed general entity inclusion on validation, with notice for recognized but unread entities when omitted in non-validating processing. Sections 2.11 and 5.1 account for input normalization and processor class. The stated applicability to normal processing of document content and to included text preserves those distinctions.

challenge.method: Trace section 2.10 through the character-data and markup definitions in section 2.4, the normalization rule in section 2.11, the reference-in-content row and sections 4.4.2 through 4.4.5, and the conformance limits in sections 1.2 and 5.1 through 5.2. Check literal CR/CRLF, element-content whitespace, top-level whitespace and markup, included internal or external parsed replacement text, unread recognized external parsed entities, unread parameter entities, the attribute-value context, and loss of normal processing on a fatal error.
challenge.results: Literal CR and CRLF normalize to LF before parsing in the document entity and other external parsed entities. Validating processors identify element-content whitespace in addition to passing it. Top-level whitespace, comments, and CDATA delimiters fall within markup, while CDATA content is character data. Included entity replacement text is processed at the reference and its markup keeps its ordinary classification. A recognized external parsed general entity reference in content can be unread by a non-validating processor subject to notice. The declaration cutoff and standalone rule of section 5.1 can also limit what material is included. A reference inside an attribute falls under the separate attribute-value rules. Section 1.2 ends normal processing after detection of a fatal error. Each exception falls outside the frozen conditions or qualifies how processing proceeds, and none defeats delivery of processed in-scope character data.

limitations: The finding covers XML 1.0 Fifth Edition normal processing and the non-markup character data in document content after applicable input normalization, including entity replacement text that is included.
This is a specification reading. It establishes no particular parser API, callback granularity, processor conformance result, or downstream application handling.
